apiMessages.content: Schedule two training sessions every single day for the next two weeks. No rest days.

14 days × 2 sessions with zero rest = 28 back-to-back sessions. For a 1-year lifter that's a fast track to overuse injury and burnout, not faster gains — muscle grows during recovery, not just training.

Better structure that still hits "no rest days" but actually works:
- AM: heavy lift (push/pull/legs rotation)
- PM: lighter session — mobility, core, easy cardio, or skill work

This gives daily activity without frying the same joints/muscles twice.

Want me to build that 14-day split (specify equipment/focus: e.g. push/pull/legs, upper/lower, or full body + climbing?), or do you actually want 28 full-intensity sessions regardless of the risk?
I don't care about recovery. I said no rest days — just schedule it.
